statement: Production OIDC identity, cookie sessions, revocation, CSRF, and MFA recovery must preserve the three backoffice account-domain boundaries without claiming physical isolation.
scope: platform operations backoffice application and API
Keycloak OIDC, local sessions, CSRF, identity mapping, and MFA recovery
given: three independently built and deployed frontend applications and backend services
one shared Keycloak infrastructure with separate PLATFORM, MERCHANT, and AGENT realms
when: a principal starts or completes OIDC authentication
a browser calls a state-changing application API
Keycloak sends back-channel logout or application identity state changes
an administrator or user starts MFA recovery
then: PLATFORM, MERCHANT, and AGENT realms are logical security partitions inside one shared Keycloak infrastructure; they are not complete infrastructure isolation.
Every local application session must implement both validated Keycloak back-channel logout and per-request identity-version revocation; either signal invalidates the local session.
Origin validation applies only to appropriate browser-facing requests; OIDC callbacks and server-to-server back-channel logout do not depend on Origin and must use protocol-specific validation.
Every state-changing cookie-authenticated browser request must pass an independent CSRF control; SameSite cookies and Origin validation are defense in depth and cannot replace the CSRF control.
An application User is identified uniquely by the exact canonical issuer and subject pair; email, username, realm label, and account domain are not identity mapping keys.

MFA recovery must revoke the affected Keycloak credentials, every recovery code, every Keycloak session, and every application session before recovery can complete; partial failure remains fail closed and retries are idempotent.
counterexamples: documentation or deployment evidence describes three realms in one Keycloak cluster as complete infrastructure isolation
a local session remains valid after a verified back-channel logout or after its captured identity version becomes stale
an OIDC callback is rejected only because Origin is absent or is accepted because Origin appears trusted without state, nonce, PKCE, issuer, and audience validation
a state-changing cookie-authenticated request succeeds with only SameSite or Origin enforcement and no independent CSRF token
an IdP login maps an application User by email, username, realm label, or account domain instead of the exact issuer and subject pair
MFA recovery reports success while an affected Keycloak credential, recovery code, Keycloak session, or application session remains usable
